newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AvH says Dredging order books full.
newsitem.headline: AvH says Dredging order books full.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ackermans & van Haaren NV (AvH) said on Tuesday the order books for its Dredging International unit were already full until 1999.
"For 1997 and 1998 the fleet is entirely occupied," AvH Chairman Erik van Baren told a news conference.
"We will have a very good year in 1997 and 1998," he said.
AvH has a 39.3 percent stake in dredging group DEME, which fully controls Dredging International and dredgers Decloedt.
Van Baren said Dredging had been focusing more on new niche markets such as dredging for the Interconnector gas pipeline.
He said those niche works now accounted for 22 percent of turnover. Works in the Far East accounted for 30 percent.
Van Baren said Belgian and Dutch dredgers now accounted for 70 percent of the world market.
AvH has repeatedly complained that Dutch dredgers were enjoying a more favourable tax regime, which was making their workers half as costly as their colleagues in Belgium.
AvH is now seeking Belgian and EU approval for a cut in social charges for Belgian dredgers to put them back at a level playing field with the Netherlands.
Chief Executive Officer Luc Bertrand said AvH would have earned nearly half a billion francs if workers had had similar wages and social charges as in the Netherlands.
